intrapersonal_axes.axis_name: From self-commanded agency to protective relational communion
intrapersonal_axes.pole_start: Begins as a self-possessed, tactically effective man oriented toward practical control, discretion, and competent management of crises from a position of relative emotional distance.
intrapersonal_axes.pole_end: Ends as a disciplined husband-father whose identity is organized around protective care, grief, forgiveness, and moral stewardship within intimate family bonds.

trajectory.position_description: He operates with strong agency: calm, businesslike, and socially masterful, handling negotiations, investigations, and domestic matters through composure and practical judgment.
key_moments: East Lynne purchase and household management
careful handling of the Hare crisis
social tact with Isabel and Barbara

trajectory.position_description: His agency increasingly serves communion as concern for Isabel deepens into rescue, proposal, and marital commitment; he becomes emotionally invested in others' vulnerability.
key_moments: financial and practical aid to Isabel

trajectory.position_description: He remains capable and controlling, but his actions are now burdened by secrecy, loyalty, and the emotional consequences of domestic entanglement, especially around Barbara, Isabel, and Levison.
key_moments: unrecognized suffering of Isabel as Madame Vine

trajectory.position_description: Fatherhood, loss, and revelation strip away any illusion of detached control; he remains authoritative, but his center of gravity is now family care, mourning, forgiveness, and the maintenance of household peace.

intrapersonal_axes.evidence_summary: Carlyle never loses agency, but the novel steadily reorients that agency toward communion. He begins as a controlled social master and ends as a morally burdened, emotionally interdependent family man.

intrapersonal_axes.axis_name: From confident practical judgment to chastened moral caution
intrapersonal_axes.pole_start: Starts with confidence in his own ability to read situations correctly through tact, evidence, and reasoned inference.
intrapersonal_axes.pole_end: Ends with a humbler, more evidence-bound and morally careful mode of knowing, aware that appearances, secrecy, and even his own perceptions can mislead him.

trajectory.position_description: He trusts his practical judgment in the Richard Hare matter and believes careful questioning and social tact can uncover the truth.
He grows more certain that hidden wrongdoing exists, but also more aware that direct accusation may be unjust and that certainty requires proof.
He insists on lawful process and refuses revenge, recognizing the danger of personal bias and the need for proper channels of justice.
key_moments: refusal to make Levison's crimes his own cause

trajectory.position_description: He must live with delayed truth and incomplete knowledge, accepting that being right is not the same as being able to prevent suffering in time.
key_moments: William's death under the shadow of past wrongs
revelation of Isabel's identity at the end of her life

intrapersonal_axes.evidence_summary: Carlyle's arc is from confident practical inference toward chastened moral caution. The novel teaches him that perception is not enough; judgment must become humble, lawful, and ethically restrained.

intrapersonal_axes.axis_name: From tactful concealment to morally necessary truth-telling
intrapersonal_axes.pole_start: Begins as a man who treats discretion, omission, and managed appearances as useful tools for preserving order and protecting others.
intrapersonal_axes.pole_end: Ends as a man who believes truth must be spoken directly, even when painful, because secrecy has moral consequences in intimate life.

trajectory.position_description: He habitually keeps matters private, conceals plans, and uses tactful omission as a social instrument.
key_moments: concealing East Lynne plans from Cornelia
managing social situations without public disclosure

trajectory.position_description: He begins to prefer direct truth when the stakes are life, death, and trust, especially in his dealings with Isabel.
key_moments: telling Isabel the truth about Mount Severn
explaining practical realities of the crisis

trajectory.position_description: His concealments around Levison and Barbara become costly, contributing to jealousy, misunderstanding, and emotional collapse.
He chooses to tell Barbara the truth himself and handles the revelation with candor, restraint, and moral seriousness.
key_moments: recognition of Isabel as Madame Vine

intrapersonal_axes.evidence_summary: Carlyle moves from using secrecy as a default instrument of control to treating truth as a moral necessity. The arc culminates in disclosure that is painful but ethically deliberate.

intrapersonal_axes.axis_name: From restrained composure to disciplined tenderness
intrapersonal_axes.pole_start: Starts emotionally contained, with affection expressed indirectly through courtesy, practical help, and controlled reserve.
intrapersonal_axes.pole_end: Ends still self-possessed, but openly capable of grief, forgiveness, and tender moral speech under the pressure of loss and revelation.

trajectory.position_description: His feelings are present but muted; he is warm without being openly vulnerable.
He becomes visibly moved by Isabel's suffering and by the possibility of losing her, though he still channels emotion into action.
Fatherhood and loss strip away any illusion of control; William's illness and death force him into helpless mourning.
He is emotionally overwhelmed by Isabel's return and death, but his defining response remains restraint: forgiveness, disclosure, and duty.

intrapersonal_axes.evidence_summary: Carlyle remains disciplined throughout, but the novel steadily exposes the cost of that discipline. His arc is toward a more vulnerable, emotionally burdened selfhood in which self-command is still central but no longer sufficient.

intrapersonal_axes.axis_name: From procedural honor to compassionate moral judgment
intrapersonal_axes.pole_start: Begins with a legalistic, orderly ethic centered on evidence, propriety, and honorable dealing.
intrapersonal_axes.pole_end: Ends with a broader moral vision that includes forgiveness, pity, Christian resignation, and the protection of the vulnerable.

trajectory.position_description: He thinks in terms of sound investment, proof, reputation, and discreet management; morality is practical and procedural.
key_moments: careful handling of witnesses and magistrates

trajectory.position_description: His moral code expands to include direct intervention on behalf of the suffering, especially Isabel; compassion becomes active duty.
He insists on lawful justice, refuses personal vengeance, and accepts that truth must be pursued through proper channels.
His moral reasoning culminates in pity, forgiveness, and religious resignation; he condemns wrongdoing while extending mercy to the fallen.

intrapersonal_axes.evidence_summary: Carlyle's morality evolves from procedural correctness into a more humane, spiritually inflected ethic. He never abandons order, but increasingly subordinates it to mercy, duty, and protection.

relational_axes.target_character: Lady Isabel Carlyle / Lady Isabel Vane
relational_axes.axis_name: From fascinated admiration to protective, wounded, and forgiving love
relational_axes.pole_start: Begins as admiration for Isabel's beauty, grace, and sadness, with a sense that she is worthy of protection but not yet fully known.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends in tragic intimacy: he loves, grieves, forgives, and preserves moral tenderness toward her even after betrayal, revelation, and death.

trajectory.position_description: He is struck by Isabel's refinement and charity, admiring her from a distance with idealizing fascination and restrained interest.
His feeling becomes intimate and urgent as he witnesses her grief and vulnerability, moving from admiration to rescue and proposal.
As husband, he is affectionate and protective, but secrecy, jealousy, and misunderstanding create emotional distance and hidden suffering.
key_moments: preparing East Lynne for her arrival

trajectory.position_description: He recognizes Madame Vine as Isabel, receives her confession, forgives her, and is left with love transformed by grief and moral memory.

relational_axes.evidence_summary: This is Carlyle's central relational arc: admiration becomes protective love, then wounded estrangement, and finally pitying forgiveness. It is the novel's most emotionally and morally consequential relationship.

relational_axes.axis_name: From warm, ambiguous kindness to secure marital partnership
relational_axes.pole_start: Begins as courteous, teasing, emotionally ambiguous warmth that invites attachment before his intentions are fully clear.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends as a devoted husband whose bond with Barbara is secure, mutually trusted, and publicly affirmed, despite the residue of past pain.

trajectory.position_description: He is kind, playful, and attentive, but not yet fully aware of the emotional meaning of his behavior.
key_moments: protective help in the Hare crisis

trajectory.position_description: Barbara's confession and Isabel's jealousy force him to confront the ambiguity of his earlier warmth; he responds with tact, apology, and emotional re-centering.
He turns decisively toward Barbara as his future wife, proposes, and consolidates the marriage with solemn trust and public commitment.
Their relationship becomes the secure center of his life: affectionate, companionate, and morally authoritative, even when tested by scandal, grief, and disclosure.
key_moments: Barbara's support during illness and politics

relational_axes.evidence_summary: Barbara moves from being the object of Carlyle's casual warmth to the chosen, stabilizing partner of his mature life. The arc is quieter than the Isabel arc, but essential to his final domestic identity.

relational_axes.axis_name: From cautious doubt to protective vindication
relational_axes.pole_start: Begins with Richard as a legal and moral problem, treated with caution and not yet trusted.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends with Carlyle firmly convinced of Richard's innocence and actively protecting him through secrecy, legal mediation, and practical support.

trajectory.position_description: He listens carefully but does not yet believe Richard; he treats him as weak and possibly guilty while testing the story.
He increasingly doubts the official story and begins to protect Richard indirectly while investigating the truth.
He shelters Richard, arranges secrecy, and works through lawful channels to clear him, refusing rash or vengeful action.
Richard's innocence is publicly confirmed, and Carlyle's long support is rewarded by the legal outcome.

relational_axes.evidence_summary: Carlyle's relation to Richard shifts from legal suspicion to active advocacy. He becomes one of the key agents of Richard's restoration, though always through restrained, lawful means.

relational_axes.axis_name: From courteous tolerance to disciplined contempt
relational_axes.pole_start: Begins with polite social accommodation and only mild unease toward a man whose danger he does not yet fully grasp.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends in firm moral condemnation and complete distrust, governed by restraint and legality rather than revenge.

trajectory.position_description: He receives Levison civilly and does not yet fully grasp the danger he represents.
He becomes increasingly wary as Thorn and Levison begin to look like the same dangerous man.
He becomes convinced of Levison's guilt and treats him as contemptible, but refuses to act from revenge.

relational_axes.evidence_summary: Levison becomes the principal external antagonist in Carlyle's moral world. The relationship hardens from social civility into principled hostility, but Carlyle's restraint keeps that hostility ethically disciplined.

relational_axes.axis_name: From family deference to firm domestic self-assertion
relational_axes.pole_start: Begins habitually deferential to Cornelia's practical authority and accustomed to her managing role.
relational_axes.pole_end: Ends respectful but clearly independent, no longer willing to let her dominate his household or decisions.

trajectory.position_description: He treats Cornelia with affection and respect, but also lets her authority shape the household by force of habit.
He hides his marriage plans and manages her tactfully, signaling that he is no longer fully governed by her expectations.
He decisively informs her she must leave East Lynne, asserting his own authority over the household.

relational_axes.evidence_summary: This quieter relational arc shows Carlyle moving from family habit and deference toward self-directed domestic authority, especially once Barbara becomes his wife.
